title: Year-end newsletter 2024–2025
summary: A four-page illustrated review of Act for Goa’s work in 2024 and 2025.
markdown:
2024-2025 has seen Act for Goa restructure to meet Goa’s changing needs and to better deliver on our MoU with the Goa State Biodiversity Board (GSBB) for communication and implementation of the Goa State Climate action plan (SAPCC).

ActforGoa has orientated all activities around

- 3 key thematic focus areas and
- 4 crosscutting workstreams

We are now better poised to support stakehodlers from across society to contribute to the interconnected goals of climate resilience, inclusive green progress and cultural and natural heritage protection.

## Conscious planning

A cross-sector initiative bringing together planners, architects, lawyers, community members, community organizers, government bodies, and businesses to explore how Goas town and country planning can integrate climate resilience and inclusive green prosperity - both at state and village levels. This initiative kicked off on November 24 with a Circlewallas hosted participatory circle, with sponsorship for venue and food costs provided.

See the workshop report and 2-month update report here.

This initiative has kickstarted

- **Legal Working Group:** looking at dymystifying planning processes and legal compliance
- **Data working group:** looking at how cutting-edge tech and data can inform and support panchayat and state-level planning
- **Village action:** pilot project in Siolim looking first at water mapping to tackle water shortages and plan for better integration of watershed management into the current planning process.
- A team working on a project proposal to prototype data-driven climate resilience planning into the Gram Panchayat Development Planning process.
- **Conscious planning framework development group:** looking at formulating a propositional Goa-specific planning process that honours the unique social and ecological context of Goa
- **Communications working group:** working on a conscious planning awareness campaign and narrative shaping.
- We are excited about this initiative and its potential to offer a different model of progress for Goa that is not about concrete urbanization. This is timely as spatial planning has just been reconfirmed as being a Panchayat responsibility.
- We will be raising funds for this important work.

## Nature conservation

In July 2024, we convened a group of nature specialists to look at how we could catalyze viable nature conservation models in the context of rising real estate prices. This group recommended:

- Working on the ground in a few villages to create model villages that can test ideas out
- Scoping social enterprise business models for land use, specifically exploring the potential of a land trust
- Creating a structure to enable co-working for the long term rather than getting stuck in short term project stop/start patterns (This informed the new AfG strategy)
- Separately through our collaboration with Goa Institute of Management we also facilitated a dashboard of traditional healers for GSBB

## Regenerative tourism

Responding to the Government’s promotion of Regenerative Tourism, we also engaged different stakeholders

- We convened international and Goa-based stakeholders to explore what was needed to scale regenerative tourism beyond niche. Participants included the Global Ecovillage Network, the Travel and Tourism Association of Goa (TTAG), and the global Sustainable Hospitality Alliance, as well as regenerative tourism stakeholders from Goa such as Make It Happen, Natures Nest, center for Responsible Tourism. The key next steps are a regenerative tourism club enabling a financial model around more conscious tourism operators; and a Spirit of Goa campaign to help tell the stories of the real Goa we know and love.
- We designed a project along with government and industry bodies to develop a shared vision of excellence in Goa and means of activating this including through standards and a group of front-runners as well as collaboration. Shortly to seek funding for this.

## Cross cutting workstreams

### Comms for behavior change

Continuing the need for simple civic information messaging and amplification of simple ways to make a difference we:

- Worked with Aware citizens of Assagao to create a citizens handbook on panchayat workings in English and Konkani.
- Translated the ActforGoa principles into Konkani
- Built a team to develop the Spirit of Goa and Give Back to Goa campaigns.
- Continued social media and WhatsApp amplifying of green activities in Goa.
- Social media this year has been less due to having no coordinator for 7 months.

### MOG x Act for Goa Series

We also hosted 6 events in partnership with MoG Sundays on 1) waste management 2) responsible tourism, 3) spirituality and ecology, 4) conscious planning 5) Marine Ecology and 6) responsible citizenship - the role of citizens in legal compliance.

Each of these events resulted in a poster of different ways that diverse stakeholders can conribute.

### Network building and collaboration

Continuing our vision of a connected network of organisations collaborating for a green climate resilient Goa, we did outreach and collaborations with a variety of stakeholders including:

- Goa Institute of Management, Goa College of Archictecture
- Radio Indigo, Herald
- Goa Pollution Control board, Goa Institute of Public Administration and Rural Development.
- Civic groups in a number of villages including Arpora, Siolim and Assagao.

### Village/place-based on ground prototypes

Ensuring our systemic State level work is grounded in ground realities, we are working on village prototypes in Siolim and Verna, with new villages to come online in 2025 once the conscious planning/date-driven village planning project is underway.

### Data and Tech

Building on the websitee that contains a green directory and resource bank of green resources, we are now building out tech and data tools to support wider participation in sustianble development.

- Working with AnAngelearth to develop the Indian AnAngel interface - a platform enabling mobilization of resources (volunteers, funding, etc) for doing good, gamified (Karmapoints redeemable at businesses), and verified monitoring with Blockchain.
- Also exploring working with the Goa remote sensing center to explore how data can support climate-resilient development.
- We are testing a mapping approach to enable mass volunteer mapping of assets and issues to support participatory sustainable development

## Acknowledgements

ActforGoa is a collaborative platform enabling stakeholders from across society to contribute to a clean, green, resilient, inclusive, and prosperous Goa, ensuring the protection of natural and cultural heritage.

Actforgoa celebrates responsible citizenship and enables collaboration across societal divides to meet the needs of our times.

ActforGoa runs on the goodwill of volunteers and has plans to further support volunteerism at scale in Goa, as well as enable the mobilisation of all kinds of other resources towards a green future for Goa.

We celebrate and remain enormously grateful to

The cofounders of ActforGoa, Dean D Cruz, Reboni Saha, Stalin K, Jessica Mayberry, Jill Ferguson, Tamer Salameh and Joanna Pyres who have supported the idea of a Goa platfrom since its inception and continue to act as Stewards of the platform in a board capacity.

Those who have stepped forward to lead ActforGoa’s next chapter of impact - Maya D Souza, Joanna Pyres, Neha Bhattia, Trella Rodrigues, and Tamer Salameh.

Those whohave/are providing advice such as Sachin Tendulkar (Mineral Foundation of Goa) Jack Sukhija (Panjim Inn & TTAG), Puja Mitra (Terra Conscious) Johann Fernandes (Climatexcapital), Nirmal Kulkarni (Madhei Research Centre), Arvind Nair (Hooop marketing) and many others.

The numerous volunteers who give their time to support positive collective action such as Abha Mehendiratta (cultural heritage) Marilyn Fernandes, (Comms) Meena Pillai (Comms) Malcolm Afonso (Data) Marlon Rodrigues (Data) Paromita (Legal) Aurobindo Gomes Perreira (Legal) Shreya Basu (events)

Those who provide financial support such as Gokhul Charity who offered a h 1L donation. Anil Rao who suponsoreed the Conscious Planning event costs. Maya D Souza who provided a 50L donation.

The 2024-2025 operating budget of ActforGoa was 3L, of which 2L was spent on coordintor salary and 1L on tech hosting and accountancy costs.

title: Taking action for Goa
summary: Community recognition, the Goa Climate Series and projects supporting the environment.
markdown:
Hello again reader!

Here’s a few highlights of how we’ve #ActedforGoa lately.

![Illustration from the original newsletter](/assets/newsletters/2022-december-0036e5abc5ab3d38.jpg)

**Act For Goa gets felicitated**

In November 2022, Act for Goa was felicitated at IFFI’s CleanAThon event among other brilliant NGO’s, organisations and Panchayats for participating and doing exemplary work for Goa’s environment.

[Read More](https://actforgoa.org/portfolio/act-for-goa-gets-felicitated/)

![Illustration from the original newsletter](/assets/newsletters/2022-december-e67a5d9b9a1eb68f.png)

**Goa Climate Series**

Act for Goa in partnership with Johann Fernandes, Prana, Terra.Do and Climate Interactive recently organised Session 2 of the Goa Climate Series where key components of the draft Goa State Action Plan on Climate Change from 2020 – 2030 were discussed and modelled it’s impact on mitigating climate change using the En-Roads simulator developed by Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), USA.

[Know More](https://actforgoa.org/goa-climate-series-an-interactive-climate-action-workshop/)

![Illustration from the original newsletter](/assets/newsletters/2022-december-494912d60a41f7d5.png)

**Infrastructure and Development in Goa**

There has been so much happening in the development sector in Goa – with various amendments and laws being passed, and the same being questioned by the citizens of state. 
We at Act for Goa have taken upon ourselves to shed some light and give an insight into some of these issues.

[Learn More & Take Action](https://actforgoa.org/goa-development-and-infrastructure-2022/)

**VOLUNTEER WITH ACT FOR GOA**

![Illustration from the original newsletter](/assets/newsletters/2022-december-670975a22f498d1c.png)

**Would you like to contribute?
Volunteer with Act for Goa!**

To dig deeper and share information in a timely manner to the public, especially with varied social and economic issues emerging in our state, we are looking for volunteers to help research such matters.

This is a self paced volunteer position and those interested may contact:

**+91 7972113952** via WhatsApp, or email **trella@actforgoa.org**.

**Help us Help you!**

ActforGoa has just published [**"A Voters Guide to the Upcoming Goa Village Panchayat Elections 2022."**](https://actforgoa.org/planning-for-development-and-infrastructure/a-voters-guide-for-goa-panchayat-elections-2022/)

title: Stay informed, take action
summary: World Environment Day clean-ups and other community initiatives around Goa.
markdown:
Welcome reader to our latest newsletter.

Act for Goa has been engaged in some interesting initiatives to help contribute to a better Goa. Scroll down to know of our latest projects.

## Act for goa community activations

![Illustration from the original newsletter](/assets/newsletters/2022-july-227a1b839112e18e.png)

## World Environment Day Clean-Up Drive Event held in North Goa

Act for Goa joined hands with organisations alike and 250 volunteers to clean up 5 different locations across North Goa on the 5th of June 2022, which is recognised as World Environment Day, an initiative that helped gather 260 bags of garbage. 

The emphasis of this venture was to honour this year’s theme ‘**Only One Earth**‘, which draws our attention towards playing our role effectively while living in perfect harmony with nature – without proving a burden on it.

[Read More](https://actforgoa.org/portfolio/world-environment-day-2022-clean-up-drive/)

![Illustration from the original newsletter](/assets/newsletters/2022-july-f5115f7f23ea927c.png)

## A Goan Eco Film festival

Act for Goa in collaboration with Jnana Foundation hosted an Eco Film Fest at Prana Anjuna featuring various films made by local artists and active citizens on issues affecting Goa’s green ecosystem. The makers ranged from students and active youth, to eminent artists and experts, while the films gave everyone a deeper insight of environmental issues around Goa, and let us know that it’s high time we citizens take action for Goa’s sustainable development.

[Read More](https://actforgoa.org/portfolio/a-goan-eco-film-festival/)

![Illustration from the original newsletter](/assets/newsletters/2022-july-2a32d298847c73d1.png)

## A Mangrave: (En)circling the loss

Mangrave: (En)circling the loss is a short film made by Act for Goa and members of The Earthvist Collective. It sheds light on the art project ‘Amchem Mangrove’, which is the collective intervention to the vast tract of Mangroves that has been systematically destroyed in Merces, Goa along the Panjim - Bambolim highway. All that remains of a once thriving Mangrove is a massive stretch of skeletal trees.

[Watch Here](https://youtu.be/NqoE2QFFTjw)

## Community spotlight
Highlighting some amazing CAMPAIGNS & INITIATIVES happening across Goa

![Illustration from the original newsletter](/assets/newsletters/2022-july-92e5c75152c08d51.png)

## GOA’S GREEN MANIFESTO

Goa’s Green Manifesto is a collaborative effort involving citizens associated with the Amche Mollem campaign, youth groups and experts in various fields, which details the changes and commitments we demand from elected representatives that are consistent with the vision of sustainable development.

As an active response to the climate crisis and towards the future well-being of the population, we urge you to read the manifesto and further sign or endorse it.

[Learn More](https://actforgoa.org/goas-green-manifesto/)

![Illustration from the original newsletter](/assets/newsletters/2022-july-108d967085cc47eb.png)

## The #MAKANAKAPLASTIC Campaign

#MakaNakaPlastic (which translates to “I do not want plastic’) is a local Goan movement aimed at providing a sustainable alternative to single use plastic.

This model conceptualised by Sensible.Earth, is to turn old clothing into upcycled reusable bags made by local women.

[Read More](https://actforgoa.org/portfolio/all-about-the-makanakaplastic-campaign/)

**Thank you for reading.**
The Act for Goa team

working towards making Goa a better place?

title: Act for Goa’s first newsletter
summary: An introduction to the shared platform and its early activities.
markdown:
![Illustration from the original newsletter](/assets/newsletters/2022-april-b3f6953eccee4d94.png)

Dear reader, Hello!

There is so much interesting content on the ActforGoa website and social media platforms, and so we decided it’s about time we start a newsletter.

You are getting this newsletter either because you were in touch with someone from the ActforGoa team, or because we believe you care deeply about Goa and are actively working for the betterment of Goa, as a business, a government department, an educator, an NGO or as a concerned citizen or resident. We promise not to write to you too frequently, and you can, of course, unsubscribe at any time from these updates. But instead we hope you will see the value in a shared platform for positive change, get involved by sharing your knowledge and work and help spread the word about ActforGoa!

So what is ActforGoa?

**Act For Goa** **is an apolitical platform that has become a space where people can access information, understand local issues, know the facts, connect with others & find accessible simple resources to take action for Goa’s sustainable development.**

Live as of November 2019, Act for Goa has

- Set up a functioning **web portal** in parallel to **social media platforms** with **resources**& **infographics**of accessible public information, a **network & directory** of people and organisations working for a clean & green Goa, **opportunities**to take action, **inspiring stories**of active citizens among other such vital information.

- Co-developed and launched the **Pinit App**with [Ninestack](https://ninestack.com/) - a functional **issue-reporting and asset-mapping app** that encourages public participation in in sustainability mapping and gives people a practical tool to support their local sustainable development journeys.

ActforGoa has identified 10 categories to guide our sustainability awareness and action, 2 of which we are yet to launch - namely Women Empowerment and Mental & Physical Well-Being, and every month we curate and create new content to shine a light on a particular theme, amplify the amazing work others are doing and share that content across our social media to raise awareness and encourage action and participation.

[![Illustration from the original newsletter](/assets/newsletters/2022-april-199a416eb6cf9bc5.png)](https://actforgoa.org/)

How can you **#actforgoa**? Be sure to follow us on Instagram and/or Facebook to see the latest events, resources from across Goa or email us at [info@actforgoa.org](mailto:info@actforgoa.org) to start a conversation about how we can showcase your work.

[![Illustration from the original newsletter](/assets/newsletters/2022-april-260701ac8c3e7613.png)](https://actforgoa.org/directory/)

## Directory of Experts and Organisations

Act for Goa started after a series of dialogues showed us that people want to easily find individuals, organisations and businesses who can help them with issues close to their heart to make Goa more sustainable.

Join our a directory or let us know who is missing!

[Learn More](https://actforgoa.org/directory/)

## Buland Bol

Buland Bol is an online course in digital video and social media for social change - an initiative by Video Volunteers and Act for Goa. Presently, Video Volunteers is training 600+ people from 21 states and has extended to Goa.

This is an opportunity for students to learn skills to help them better understand and communicate the pulse of their State and the unnerving realities of unsustainable progress and realise the ecosystem of citizen journalism.

[![Illustration from the original newsletter](/assets/newsletters/2022-april-283f229c91ad9f30.png)](https://www.videovolunteers.org/buland-bol-free-media-training/)

[Learn More](https://www.videovolunteers.org/buland-bol-free-media-training/)

![Illustration from the original newsletter](/assets/newsletters/2022-april-5ca1e955dd70950f.png)

## ActforGoa’s Fellowship programme with Cecille Rodrigues

To launch the Pinit app, ActforGoa partnered with and provided a fellowship to Goa’s road safety warrior Cecille Rodrigues, to amplify the campaign to get citizens to ‘pin’ potholes and traffic hazards in their locality.

A number of locals from various villages participated and a comprehensive map and report for Taleigao was submitted to the Village Panchayat to incorporate into Village development planning

[Learn More](https://actforgoa.org/road-safety-in-goa/)

## Thank you for reading.

The ActforGoa Team

Follow us on our socials

Please do forward this email to like minded people like you so that they can subscribe, and please be in touch if you would like to.
